input.prompt: The nameplate illustration of a mid-century American Sunday newspaper colour comics section, a wide horizontal composition across the middle of the frame: a long blank cream scroll banner with curled ends stretched across the whole width, held up at its left end by a cheerful cartoon bull standing on his hind legs and at its right end by a grumpy cartoon bear standing on his hind legs, both with big gloved cartoon hands, a curling ribbon of blank stock ticker tape looping around the banner and the two animals, a few small gold coins tumbling, against a sunny yellow printed tint with coarse red Ben-Day dots fading to the edges. The banner's face is completely empty and smooth. Drawing style: confident brush-and-nib black ink line with thick and thin strokes, flat process colour from a limited palette of cyan, magenta, yellow and black tints printed on warm yellowed newsprint, visible coarse Ben-Day dot screens, a hair of colour misregistration, newsprint grain. Not a photo, not 3D, not anime. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no signs with writing, no speech balloons, no panel borders.
